title: Triple Trouble: The Final Capture Choice
summary: Compare the resulting bishop and queen diagrams: taking the same checking queen can either preserve a win or cause stalemate.

nodes.question: Which answer to the queen check keeps the win?
nodes.explanation: Begin after ...Qxd4+ in the bishop-promotion variation. White has Kb6, Be6 and Bh8 against Ka3, Qd4 and pawns a4/e7. White must answer the queen check.

nodes.question: Would a queen on h8 give the same result?
nodes.explanation: This separately pictured seven-piece diagram has Qh8 instead of Bh8. The extra queen’s control changes whether Black has a legal reply after capture.

branches.title: The promoted bishop captures
commentary: Begin after ...Qxd4+ in the bishop-promotion variation. White has Kb6, Be6 and Bh8 against Ka3, Qd4 and pawns a4/e7. White must answer the queen check.

Bxd4 answers the check and removes the queen. Black can still play ...Kb4, so this is not stalemate. White has two bishops against two pawns and retains an exact win; the longer conversion is outside this short branch.

branches.title: The queen capture stalemates
commentary: Compare the queen-promotion version of the same checking sacrifice.
Qxd4 is stalemate. Qd4 controls a4 and b4; Be6 controls a2 and b3; Kb6 controls a5 and b5. Ka3 is not checked, a4 is blocked by the king on a3 and e7 is blocked by Be6 on e6. Black has no legal move.
branches.explanation: Qxd4 is stalemate. Qd4 controls a4 and b4; Be6 controls a2 and b3; Kb6 controls a5 and b5. Ka3 is not checked, a4 is blocked by the king on a3 and e7 is blocked by Be6 on e6. Black has no legal move.

branches.title: Independent king escape loses the win
commentary: Begin after ...Qxd4+ in the bishop-promotion variation. White has Kb6, Be6 and Bh8 against Ka3, Qd4 and pawns a4/e7. White must answer the queen check.
Ka5 evades check without removing the queen, but this exact position is losing for White. Bxd4 is the only legal move preserving the win in the supported diagram.

exercises.prompt: Why is the queen capture safe with a bishop on h8?
exercises.answer: After Bxd4, the black king still has b4. A queen on d4 would control that square and finish the stalemate cage.

exercises.prompt: Why can Black not simply advance e7?
exercises.answer: Black’s e7 pawn cannot move forward because White’s bishop occupies e6. A pawn cannot capture the piece directly in front of it.

startContext: Only the seven-piece endings after ...Qxd4+ are checked here: the bishop variation at 118s and queen variation at 76s. The earlier nine/eight-piece promotion decision and triple-bishop mating variations remain source context. This lesson verifies the final capture and stalemate contrast rather than claiming an exact proof of the larger underpromotion setup.
